en.name: Pesto, jarred
en.summary: Jarred pesto is basil, oil, cheese, nuts and garlic — a fresh, low-acid, dairy-containing sauce that belongs in the fridge. Unopened it keeps about 6 months from purchase, refrigerated. Once opened it is startlingly short-lived: 3 days. It freezes for about 1 month.
en.pantry: There is no room-temperature timeline for pesto, and none should be improvised. It contains fresh basil, cheese and raw garlic under oil — low-acid ingredients in an oxygen-poor environment — which is not a combination to leave on a warm counter. Keep the jar cold from the shop to the fridge, and do not leave an opened jar out while a pan of pasta boils. If a jar is sold from a shelf rather than a chilled cabinet, follow the label it came with until it is opened, then refrigerate it.
en.fridge: Keep pesto at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Unopened it runs about 6 months from purchase; once opened, only 3 days. That drop surprises people, but pesto is a fresh sauce, not a preserve — there is no vinegar, very little salt and a good deal of dairy. Level the surface and keep a film of olive oil over it to slow the browning, use a clean spoon every time, and never return pesto from a bowl of pasta to the jar.
en.freezer: Pesto freezes for about 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F), which is the practical way to handle a jar you cannot finish in three days. Freeze it in ice-cube trays the day you open it, then bag the cubes; one cube is roughly a single portion of pasta. Frozen food held at that temperature stays safe indefinitely, so the limit is flavour — and basil aroma is exactly what fades. Cheese-free pesto freezes best; stir the cheese in after thawing if you are making your own.
en.thawing: Thaw pesto cubes in the fridge, or stir them straight into hot drained pasta where they will melt. Do not thaw a jar on the counter, and do not boil pesto — heat kills the fresh basil flavour.
spoilage: A dark brown or blackened surface with an off, stale smell
Mould spots anywhere in the jar or around the rim
A rancid, crayon-like smell from the oil or the pine nuts
A fermented or fizzy character, or a lid that has domed up
tips: Freeze the jar in cubes on the day you open it — three days is very short.
Keep a film of olive oil over the surface to slow browning.
Use a clean spoon and never return sauce from the pasta bowl.
Buy small jars; a large one is false economy at this timeline.

faq.q: How long does jarred pesto last once opened?
faq.a: 3 days refrigerated at 4 °C or below. It is a fresh sauce with cheese and raw garlic in it, not a preserve.
Yes, about 1 month at −18 °C. Ice-cube trays are the practical format, and one cube is roughly a portion.

faq.q: How long does an unopened jar of pesto keep?
faq.a: About 6 months from purchase, refrigerated at 4 °C or below.

faq.q: Why does my pesto turn brown on top?
faq.a: Basil oxidises when exposed to air. It is a colour change rather than spoilage; a film of olive oil over the surface slows it.

zh.name: 罐裝青醬
zh.summary: 罐裝青醬是羅勒、油、起司、堅果和大蒜做成的——新鮮、低酸、含乳製品，本來就該放冰箱。未開封冷藏，從購買日起算大約 6 個月。開封後短得驚人：3 天。冷凍大約 1 個月。
zh.pantry: 青醬沒有常溫保存的天數，也不該憑空補一個。它含新鮮羅勒、起司和生蒜，而且浸在油裡——低酸性食材處在缺氧環境，這個組合不適合擺在溫暖的檯面上。從賣場到冰箱都要保持低溫，煮義大利麵時也不要讓開封的罐子一直擱在外面。如果某款是放在常溫貨架而不是冷藏櫃販售的，未開封時依它自己的標示，開封後一律冷藏。
zh.fridge: 青醬請放 4 °C 以下。未開封從購買日起算大約 6 個月；一旦開封就只有 3 天。這個落差常讓人意外，但青醬是新鮮醬料而不是保存品——沒有醋、鹽也很少，還含不少乳製品。請把表面抹平、蓋一層橄欖油減緩褐變，每次都用乾淨的湯匙，而且拌過麵的青醬絕對不要倒回罐子。
zh.freezer: 青醬在 −18 °C 冷凍大約 1 個月，這是處理「三天內吃不完」最實際的做法。開罐當天就用製冰盒凍成小塊再裝袋，一塊大約就是一人份義大利麵的量。食物在這個溫度下安全性可以無限期維持，所以限制的是風味——而最先流失的正是羅勒香氣。不含起司的青醬最耐凍；自己做的話，起司等解凍後再拌入。
zh.thawing: 青醬冰塊請放冷藏解凍，或直接拌進瀝乾的熱麵裡讓它化開。不要把整罐放室溫解凍，也不要把青醬煮滾——加熱會毀掉新鮮羅勒的香氣。
spoilage: 表面轉成深褐或發黑，並帶有陳味
罐內或瓶口周圍出現霉點
油或松子發出油耗味、蠟筆味
出現發酵味或氣泡感，或蓋子鼓起
tips: 開罐當天就分裝成小塊冷凍——三天真的很短。
表面蓋一層橄欖油，減緩褐變。
用乾淨的湯匙，拌過麵的絕不倒回去。
買小罐；以這個期限來看，大罐並不划算。

faq.q: 罐裝青醬開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 放 4 °C 以下冷藏 3 天。它是含起司和生蒜的新鮮醬料，不是保存品。
可以，−18 °C 大約 1 個月。用製冰盒最實用，一塊大約就是一人份。

faq.q: 未開封的青醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏在 4 °C 以下，從購買日起算大約 6 個月。

faq.q: 青醬表面為什麼會變褐色？
faq.a: 羅勒接觸空氣會氧化。那是顏色變化而不是腐壞；表面蓋一層橄欖油可以減緩。
